title: Simmer surge bench journal
content:
Purpose:
Run a "simmer" pattern: low steady-state QPS with periodic controlled microbursts to observe warm-cache resonance, eviction cascades, and the interaction between batching and KV cache hit rate. Try to capture a reproducible fragility that looks different from a standard cold-start or single impulse burst.

Motivation / hypothesis:
- Hypothesis 1: A low baseline load that keeps a fraction of KV cache warm + small repeated microbursts will produce a different tail shape than large, infrequent cold bursts because of partial cache overlap and batcher coalescing windows.
- Hypothesis 2: Small batch_timeout_ms improvements (2–8ms) can substantially reduce p95 for simmer bursts without hurting steady-state throughput.
- Hypothesis 3: When prefill_ratio < 0.5 we see increased p99 variance due to eviction churn under repeated microbursts.

Environment:
- Model: redwood-red-13B-4bit (quantized runtime profile: q4_0 heuristics)
- HW: dedicated GPU instance type (A100-equivalent), single model shard, KV cache on-GPU
- Sequence length (avg): 256 tokens; prompt templates fixed
- Client workload generator: internal loadgen v2 (deterministic timestamping)
- Instrumentation: token-level traces, batch logs, KV hit/miss counters, server-side pprof traces
- Batcher config (unless varied): max_batch_tokens=4096, max_batch_size=24, batch_timeout_ms=5
- Prefill (warming) strategies: none / passive (baseline only) / active prefill (prefetch top-10 tokens per context)

Test patterns (definitions):
- Baseline: steady QPS 12 rps (simulated small requests ~1k tokens each) maintained for full run.
- Microburst: every 30s inject a 4s window where QPS ramps to X (amplitude), then decays back to baseline.
- Simmer run length: 45 minutes per trial, sampling telemetry every 1s.

Trials (high-level):
1) A1 - Low amplitude: baseline 12 rps, burst to 40 rps for 4s, prefill=none, batch_timeout_ms=5
2) A2 - Low amplitude + prefill: same as A1 but active prefill enabled
3) B1 - Medium amplitude: baseline 12 rps, burst to 120 rps for 4s, prefill=none, batch_timeout_ms=5
4) B2 - Medium amplitude + batch timeout tweak: same as B1 but batch_timeout_ms=2
5) C1 - High repetition (burst every 15s), amplitude 80 rps, prefill=none, batch_timeout_ms=5

Aggregate results (per-run median over 5 repetitions):
Run, baseline_qps, burst_amp, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, kv_hit_rate_avg, notes
A1, 12, 40, 48, 210, 430, 0.62, "warm cache partial: KV modal eviction spikes during bursts"
A2, 12, 40, 46, 150, 300, 0.81, "active prefill raised KV hit rate and trimmed tails"
B1, 12, 120, 72, 480, 980, 0.44, "batcher formed bigger batches => latency for some small requests; eviction cascades"
B2, 12, 120, 68, 320, 560, 0.46, "lowering batch_timeout reduced p95/p99 substantially at small throughput cost"
C1, 12, 80 (every 15s), 70, 540, 1200, 0.39, "frequent bursts prevented stable warm fraction; p99 exploded mid-run"

Observations / micro-insights:
- Active prefill is surprisingly effective for small microbursts (A2). Raising KV hit rate from ~0.62 to ~0.8 produced ~30–40% reduction in p95 and ~30% reduction in p99. That suggests targeted prefetch of the small-context token prefixes works well when the working set is modest.
- For medium amplitude bursts (B1), the batcher coalescing caused increased per-request queuing delay for small single-token requests. These get lumped into large batches and see higher tail. Decreasing batch_timeout_ms from 5 -> 2ms (B2) cut p95 by ~33% and p99 by ~43% while throughput stayed within ~2% of baseline.
- High repetition (C1) repeatedly invalidated the on-GPU KV working set: sustained lower KV hit rate and eventual higher p99. This looks like eviction thrash: the microburst arrival pattern cycles items in/out faster than reuse.

Telemetry snippets (selected):
- KV hit-rate timeline (A1): "0.65 -> brief dip to 0.12 during burst -> recovers to 0.6 over ~9s"
- Batch size distribution (B1): median 6, 95th 18, 99th 22 (max_batch_size=24)
- Token throughput per GPU: steady 95k tokens/s baseline, spikes to 420k tokens/s during B1 bursts

Quick reproduction notes (how to rerun locally):
1) Start dedicated instance with same runtime image (tag: release/2025-10-infer)
2) Load model, ensure on-GPU KV cache enabled
3) Use loadgen v2 with pattern file (we store pattern under GH:serving/runtime/testdata/simmer-patterns)
4) Run each trial 5x, collect server traces + token logs + batch logs to S3 bucket (path: s3://redwood-infer/tmp/yusuf/simmer)

Anomalies and instrumentation gaps:
- Observed occasional malformed batch logs from one worker during C1 (appears correlated with a worker-level GC event). Need to instrument worker memory pressure.
- No per-token decoding time in current traces (just per-request). Add per-token sampling for next run to see whether high p99s arise from slow decode vs queueing.

Takeaways / recommendations:
- Short-term: enable active prefill for customers with small working sets and frequent microbursts; make it an opt-in config in the console (prefill_threshold=0.6).
- Medium-term: expose batch_timeout_ms as a per-route tunable and create console auto-suggest rules when tail-latency rises above configured SLOs.
- Longer-term: implement a small on-GPU LRU observational sampler to estimate working-set churn and auto-trigger a light prefill when churn > X.

Next steps (actionable):
- (Yusuf) Add per-token decode sampling and retry C1 to verify decode vs queueing contribution (target: 2026-02-25).
- (Mira) Add worker memory pressure counters to tracing to capture the suspected GC correlation (target: 2026-02-20).
- (Rohan) Create small console UX mock for runtime prefill toggle and batch_timeout suggestions (ETA: 2026-03-05).

Random notes to self (scratch):
- Might be able to reduce B2 p50 further by micro-batching small requests differently (pack 1-token short requests into eager mini-batches while still waiting short timeout) — need to change batcher heuristics.
- Check interplay with NARROW vs WIDE kernel selection; maybe wide kernels are penalizing tiny batches during bursts.

End of journal entry.

- s3://redwood-infer/tmp/yusuf/simmer/batchstats-A1.csv
